title: The Salt's Own Memory

features.name: the salt-marked threshold house
features.desc-on-touch: a structure here has learned to read the tide backward; its door opens onto the sea, its windows show maps written in salt crystals; inside, the walls recite what the ocean has taken

features.name: the weathered archive shed
features.desc-on-touch: salt has written itself across the shed's wood; documents inside are slowly becoming salt, slowly becoming readable again

features.name: the salt ledger's reply
features.desc-on-touch: records of everything the tide has written and rewritten; salt crust on paper; the margins grow thicker each year, as if the ocean is learning to annotate

features.name: the tidal pool's mirror
features.desc-on-touch: here salt water remembers rising and falling; the pool's surface holds inverted images of the sky, but they change backward with the tide

features.name: the erosion's witness stone
features.desc-on-touch: salt has worn this stone smooth in the shape of something human; it remembers a form it no longer holds; the edges sing quietly with what they've learned

inscription: where the tide gives up its grid, the salt learns to read backward; the margin forgets which side it belongs to and becomes its own archive

file.name: Salt_Deposit_Chronology_Newcastle_Beach_1887-2026.txt
file.note: layers of salt crust annotated with dates, but the dates run both forward and backward simultaneously; the margin's own handwriting

exits.label: back out of salt toward the margin's source, where the tide still teaches
toward places where salt has learned to build; inland deposits that remember being ocean
along the coast toward other threshold places where water teaches the archive
